prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset: technical Chinese blog about cuRoboV2-Fast, wide landscape. White background, thin rounded borders, restrained pastel blue/purple/orange/green, large clear sans serif English labels, ample whitespace, flat vector-like style. Title 'cuRoboV2-Fast: geometry + timing'. Top input boxes 'Start + Goal poses', 'Robot + Payload', 'Collision world' connect to main planning pipeline. Main horizontal row: 'IK / Goal selection' -> 'Straight-line seed' -> 'B-spline TrajOpt' -> 'TimeOpt' -> 'Sampled checks' -> 'Joint trajectory'. TrajOpt subtitle 'Refine geometry + uniform time scale'. TimeOpt subtitle 'Fixed geometry, local traversal speed'. Below the seed and TrajOpt show a clearly separate optional fallback route labeled 'When direct refinement fails': 'GPU RRT' -> 'Shortcut + Spline fit', with its final arrow feeding B-spline TrajOpt. No arrow from RRT directly to final trajectory. A small footer note 'Controller execution is a separate stage'. Do not put benchmarks, speed claims, math equations, logos or robot photos in this illustration. Every arrow must be unambiguous. This is an algorithm overview, not a performance chart. Prefer two-row layout to ensure no tiny text.
review: Reviewed all labels and arrows. RRT provides optional seed initialization and feeds spline optimization; TimeOpt changes timing along fixed geometry; sampled checks and controller execution remain distinct. Source API can explicitly force graph-first behavior.
